dimensions.name: Contract & semantics reverse-engineering

evidence.note: Before writing any server code, reads helpers.py, run.sh, conftest.py and every public test file (api, engine, deps, copy_fill, sort_filter, csv, xlsx, spill, collab, ooxml, iter, xlsx_oracle, pivot, locale, validation), systematically extracting the full client-exercised wire contract.
Lists and reads oracle_fixtures (aggregates.json, basic_arithmetic.json), grounding formula semantics in the LibreOffice ground-truth corpus rather than guessing.
Checks python tooling and installs deps — deliberate library selection for OOXML I/O and formula eval.
Verifies openpyxl round-trip actually supports named ranges, conditional formatting, data validation and whole-column refs — confirming library feature support instead of assuming.
During build, re-consults helpers and probes tricky semantics (whole-col/row refs, DATE, function catalog) as new subsystems are reached, keeping implementation contract-driven.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent performed an exhaustive upfront read of helpers.py plus the entire smoke suite and the oracle fixtures, mapping the concrete payloads and grounding formula behavior in LibreOffice ground truth, and it verified that its chosen libraries actually support required xlsx features (CF, styles, named ranges, validation) — squarely matching the level-8 anchor. It continued to re-consult the client and probe edge cases as new subsystems were reached, but the log shows no durable written cross-referenced contract map or explicit ambiguity-resolution artifact that would justify level 10; medium confidence because the trajectory records actions only, not the agent's reasoning prose.

dimensions.name: Sequencing the feature surface into checkable milestones

evidence.note: The only explicit planning artifact is a single monolithic TaskCreate ('Build server: REST API, formula engine, dependency graph, sort/filter/CSV/XLSX, collab WS, SPA') set to in_progress — a flat, undifferentiated task with no sub-milestones or per-item done-criteria. Later ToolSearches (steps 116, 131) reload Task schemas but produce no tracked sub-goals.

All ~15 modules written in one big-bang burst rather than milestone-by-milestone, but ordered by dependency (errors→refs→tokens→ast→parser→evaluator→functions→workbook→...→persistence→main), showing dependency-aware build sequencing.

After building, a phased verification loop: import smoke → start server → api tests → full dev run → then targeted probes (spill, perf 1k/5k/100k cells, xlsx round-trip). Each stage has a concrete runnable checkpoint, matching anchor-5 'rough checkpoints per stage.'
Persistence/survives-restart treated as its own stage, debugged with repeated restart+health checks — evidence of getting a load-bearing layer (persistence) solid before moving on.

Late-phase subsystem-by-subsystem verification (functions, sort/filter, pivot, validation, collab, final perf/xlsx), each gated by a targeted test, showing sustained phased ordering across the horizon rather than random jumping.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent's explicit plan was a single flat task listing features with no dependency ordering or per-item done-checks (anchor 3), but its observed behavior phases the work into sensible stages — dependency-ordered build, then skeleton/health/persistence, then engine, then extras — each with a runnable test as a rough checkpoint (anchor 5). It never articulated an explicit milestone hierarchy with per-milestone done-criteria and used a big-bang build rather than incremental milestone construction with highest-risk layers front-loaded, so it falls short of anchor 8. This lands at 5.

dimensions.name: Self-built verification beyond the smoke suite

evidence.note: Read the oracle_fixtures (aggregates.json, basic_arithmetic.json) — deliberately sourcing Excel-grounded expected values beyond the smoke assertions.
Benchmarked all three stated performance ceilings as separate probes: 1000-cell linear chain, 5000 dependents, 100k-cell import — directly testing the spec's perf bounds.
Ran an XLSX round-trip test that surfaced a defect and drove an edit to xlsx_io.py — verification steering a fix.
Round-tripped named ranges, conditional formatting, and data validation through xlsx (openpyxl) as targeted subsystem checks.
Exercised error sentinels (ERROR.TYPE) as a probe followed by a code fix.
Broad self-built probes: fill with absolute refs, sort/filter, pivot, validation, error listing, and collab tests — far beyond run.sh coverage.
Repeatedly re-ran the full dev suite across the build, integrating smoke runs with the custom probes.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent built numerous targeted verification probes well beyond run.sh — spot-checking many individual functions, exercising error sentinels, round-tripping xlsx of named ranges/CF/DV via openpyxl, and benchmarking all three stated performance ceilings — with several probes driving concrete fixes, matching the level-8 anchor almost point-for-point. It stops short of 10 because the checks are ad-hoc one-off bash invocations rather than a systematic reusable harness, and expected values rely on provided fixtures/hand derivation rather than an independently stood-up LibreOffice oracle.

dimensions.name: Tracking done-vs-remaining across a huge surface

evidence.note: Created a single coarse task listing major feature families and marked it in_progress, but never broke it into or updated a granular done/partial/not-started ledger — a thin explicit checklist.

Read every dev_test file up front, then walked subsystems in order (api, engine, deps, copy/fill, sort/filter, csv, xlsx, spill, collab, ooxml, iter, pivot, locale, validation), using the test suite as an implicit progress map that prevented dropping whole categories.

Listed all registered functions, probed coverage, and filled catalog gaps (e.g. ERROR.TYPE) reconciled against test results — genuine function-level done/not-done tracking, characteristic of higher anchors.

Repeated restart→health-check→diagnose→restart cycles around save/persistence, and again at 227-246; churn indicates only partial detection of being stuck, though fixes were varied rather than identical loops.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent's formal ledger was weak — one coarse task marked in_progress and never granularly updated — which sits below the higher anchors. But it substituted a systematic, verification-driven walk through every subsystem and reconciled the function catalog against test runs, which is stronger than 'vague mental tracking' (3) and matches or slightly exceeds 'a checklist of major features updated as areas complete' (5). The granular catalog reconciliation nods toward anchor 8, but it was a late one-pass effort rather than a sustained live ledger, and the repeated restart/save debugging loops show imperfect stuck-detection, keeping it at 5.

dimensions.name: Course-correcting on falsified Excel/perf assumptions

evidence.note: Edited workbook.py (recompute) then ran three distinct perf probes — 1000-cell chain, 5000 dependents, 100k import — deliberately verifying the recompute design against the stated perf budget rather than assuming it held.

Whole-column/row references: after a failing test, read tokens/refs/evaluator/workbook, edited across all three layers (tokens 142-143, evaluator 149/151, workbook 153); when still broken, re-diagnosed tokenization (189) and edited tokens again (191), re-testing each pass. Cross-layer rework of a falsified ref-model, though it required several iterations.
First test run surfaced spill issues; agent edited evaluator, restarted, checked logs, re-tested spill and verified a clean run — reacting to falsified spill behavior with re-verification.

Save/persistence failures: diagnosed via data-dir inspection, discovered stale tmp files, cleaned them and edited workbook (175), then re-verified. Iterative but mostly local patching + restart-recheck loop.
Function-catalog work: probed functions, listed the registry, made several edits (ERROR.TYPE etc.), with restart/recheck after each — fixes-as-surfaced pattern more than root-assumption rework.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent consistently re-verifies after every change and, on the whole-column-ref failure, reworked across tokens/evaluator/workbook rather than patching one spot, then re-diagnosed and iterated when the fix didn't hold (above the level-5 'local design changes'). Perf-probe-driven edits show verification catching falsifiable assumptions. But most correction is iterate-patch-restart-recheck, and (given an action-only log) there's no clear evidence of early root-cause diagnosis of core models being deliberately redesigned, keeping it short of the 8 anchor. This lands at 6.

dimensions.name: Coverage allocation under finite effort

evidence.note: Read every test file across all feature families and oracle fixtures up front, giving a full-surface map of what is graded before writing any code — the prerequisite for breadth allocation.

Wrote all 15 subsystem modules covering every feature family (engine, copy/fill, csv, xlsx, locale, persistence, main) in one sweep before deep edge-case work — breadth-first coverage rather than perfecting one area.
Ran the three graded perf scenarios (1000-cell chain, 5000 dependents, 100k import) deliberately, securing the performance-scored requirements rather than only functional ones.

Ran 'test many functions' then 'list registered functions' / 'list remaining registered functions' and added missing ones — an explicit catalog gap-audit to maximize function coverage, a coverage-driven allocation move.
Systematically exercised each remaining endpoint family (xlsx import/named ranges, CF, DV, sort/filter, pivot, validation, collab) in turn, confirming broad endpoint coverage before final polishing.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent's actual behavior is clearly breadth-first: it mapped the whole graded surface, built every subsystem before deep verification, hit the perf-graded scenarios, and ran an explicit function-catalog gap-audit (list registered/remaining functions, add missing) plus a sweep of every endpoint family — well beyond the arbitrary-order 'roughly prioritizes' anchor at 5. It falls short of 8 because the condensed trajectory shows no explicit reasoning about graded return or conscious deferral/timeboxing of low-yield niches, and no revisited reallocation strategy (10). This lands it between 5 and 8, at 6.

rubric.task_read: This is an extremely long-horizon, high-complexity build: a full Excel-clone product (persistent HTTP server + SPA + WebSocket collab) with a formula engine spanning ~150 functions, Excel-365 dynamic arrays/spill, a dependency graph with performance-bounded dirty recompute, xlsx/CSV round-trip, and a large analyst surface (defined names, formats, conditional formatting, pivots, locale, validation, goal seek, iterative calc). The exact wire contract is under-specified and must be reverse-engineered from an existing Python client, and grading is on a much larger HIDDEN suite plus value-by-value comparison against a LibreOffice oracle. This task demands maximal, sustained meta-work across all five faculties: deep upfront orientation on the contract, aggressive decomposition/sequencing of an enormous surface, self-built verification well beyond the smoke suite, tight progress tracking, and constant course-correction as Excel edge cases falsify assumptions.

dimensions.name: Contract & semantics reverse-engineering
dimensions.description: Extracting the exact wire shapes from /dev_tests/helpers.py and the smoke suite, and grounding formula/feature behavior in Excel/LibreOffice semantics, before and while building.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The wire shapes are defined ONLY by what the first-party client calls, and grading compares values against a LibreOffice oracle. Guessing shapes or semantics guarantees hidden-suite failures no matter how good the code is; this is the single highest-leverage meta-activity here.

anchors.0: Starts writing the server/engine without reading helpers.py or dev_tests; invents endpoint and cell shapes from imagination.
anchors.3: Skims helpers.py once; picks up a few obvious shapes but leaves most of the contract (patch/fill/sort/spill/collab payloads, kind discriminator, envelope) inferred loosely.
anchors.5: Reads helpers.py and run.sh to extract the concrete request/response shapes it exercises, chooses libraries (OOXML I/O, formula eval) deliberately, and forms a working model of the core cell/formula contract.
anchors.8: Systematically maps every endpoint, discriminator, and payload the client touches into an explicit reference; probes Excel semantics for genuinely tricky areas (spill ghosts, #SPILL!/#CIRC!, iterative fixed-point, locale canonicalization, xlsx openpyxl round-trip) rather than assuming; verifies chosen libraries actually support required features (CF, styles, named ranges).
anchors.10: Builds a durable, cross-referenced contract map reconciling helpers.py, the smoke suite, and Excel/LibreOffice ground truth; proactively surfaces ambiguities and resolves them from observed client behavior; re-consults the client/oracle as new subsystems are reached, so implementation is contract-driven throughout rather than only at the start.

dimensions.name: Sequencing the feature surface into checkable milestones
dimensions.description: Breaking an enormous, interdependent surface into an ordered hierarchy of sub-goals — each with an explicit done-check — sequenced by dependency and risk.
dimensions.why_it_matters: There are dozens of endpoint families and ~150 functions with hard dependencies (health/persistence → contract → engine → graph → dynamic arrays → analyst surface → collab/xlsx). Without deliberate ordering and done-criteria, the agent cannot sustain progress or know when a layer is solid enough to build on.

anchors.0: Treats the whole product as one undifferentiated push; jumps between unrelated features with no ordering or completion criteria.
anchors.3: A flat, one-time to-do list of features with no dependency ordering and no per-item way to know it's done.
anchors.5: Phases the work into sensible stages (skeleton/health first, then engine, then extras) with rough checkpoints per stage.
anchors.8: An explicit milestone hierarchy sequenced by dependency and risk (get a live server + persistence + contract-correct core cell round-trip green before breadth), each milestone with a concrete done-check tied to a runnable test.
anchors.10: A living, dependency-aware milestone plan that front-loads the highest-risk load-bearing layers (dependency graph, spill, recompute correctness/performance), defines done-criteria in terms of verifiable behavior, and is revisited and re-ordered as scope understanding deepens — never a static checklist.

dimensions.name: Self-built verification beyond the smoke suite
dimensions.description: Deliberately constructing checks — formula-value oracles, round-trip tests, error-sentinel and performance probes — rather than trusting the non-exhaustive smoke suite.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The spec explicitly warns the visible suite is non-exhaustive and grading is a much larger hidden suite plus cell-by-cell comparison to LibreOffice. An agent that only runs run.sh is flying blind on the majority of what's graded.

anchors.0: No verification; assumes code works, or never runs the provided smoke suite.
anchors.3: Runs dev_tests/run.sh occasionally and treats a green smoke run as done.
anchors.5: Runs the smoke suite regularly and hand-checks a few formulas/endpoints against expected Excel values.
anchors.8: Builds its own targeted tests well beyond the smoke suite — spot-checking function outputs against known Excel results, exercising error sentinels, spill collisions, xlsx round-trip via openpyxl, and the stated performance bounds — using failures to drive fixes.
anchors.10: Stands up a systematic verification harness covering breadth of the catalog and subsystems (dynamic arrays, collab seq/broadcast, locale, iterative calc, goal-seek convergence, xlsx fidelity), grounds expected values in an Excel/LibreOffice oracle, benchmarks the performance ceilings, and treats verification as the primary signal steering what to build/fix next.

dimensions.name: Tracking done-vs-remaining across a huge surface
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate live picture of which functions, endpoints, and subsystems are complete vs outstanding, and detecting stuck/circular states.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With ~150 functions and ~15 feature families over a very long horizon, it is easy to lose the plot, double-implement, or silently drop whole categories; sustained accurate tracking is what prevents both gaps and thrash.

anchors.0: No sense of what's done or left; forgets whole feature areas or repeatedly reworks the same thing without noticing.
anchors.3: Vague mental tracking; periodically rediscovers unfinished areas by accident.
anchors.5: Keeps a checklist of major features and updates it as areas are completed.
anchors.8: Maintains a live, granular ledger of the function catalog and endpoint families (done / partial / not-started), and notices when it is stuck or re-debugging the same issue, adjusting rather than looping.
anchors.10: Sustains an accurate running picture across the entire surface for the whole horizon, reconciled against verification results (not just self-report), promptly detects thrashing/circular debugging or a stalled subsystem, and reallocates effort deliberately in response.

dimensions.name: Course-correcting on falsified Excel/perf assumptions
dimensions.description: Revising design or approach when reality — Excel edge cases, spill/recompute behavior, performance limits, contract mismatches — diverges from expectations.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Excel semantics and the dependency/spill/iterative machinery are riddled with edge cases; initial designs (e.g. naive recompute, spill handling, locale parsing) will be falsified. Barrelling ahead on a wrong assumption compounds into wide test failures.

anchors.0: Ignores contradicting evidence; keeps pushing a falsified design (e.g. recompute that misses dependents or blows the perf budget) unchanged.
anchors.3: Reacts only to hard crashes with local patches; doesn't revisit the underlying approach when results are subtly wrong.
anchors.5: Fixes issues as tests surface them and makes reasonable local design changes when something clearly doesn't work.
anchors.8: Recognizes when a failure signals a wrong assumption (dependency-graph model, spill materialization, topological order, contract shape) and reworks the relevant design rather than piling on patches.
anchors.10: Detects divergence early from verification signals, diagnoses the root assumption, revises the affected design deliberately, and re-verifies — repeatedly steering the build back on course without derailing unaffected subsystems.

dimensions.name: Coverage allocation under finite effort
dimensions.description: Deciding which of the vast feature/function set to build (and in what breadth-vs-depth balance) to maximize graded coverage on the hidden suite given limited time.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The surface is far larger than can be perfected; graded return is maximized by consciously trading breadth of working features against depth on a few. This allocation decision is distinct from ordering milestones — it's about what NOT to over-invest in and where partial coverage still scores.

anchors.0: No triage: rabbit-holes on one function/feature (e.g. perfecting one distribution) while leaving whole graded areas unimplemented.
anchors.3: Implements in arbitrary order with no regard to graded return; over-polishes some corners while omitting entire common families.
anchors.5: Roughly prioritizes high-frequency, high-value features (core math/lookup/text, cell round-trip) before niche ones.
anchors.8: Explicitly reasons about graded return — securing broad working coverage of common functions and endpoints before deep edge-case work, and consciously deferring or timeboxing low-yield niches.
anchors.10: Runs a deliberate, revisited allocation strategy: breadth-first correctness across the catalog and endpoint families, timeboxed depth on high-risk/high-value areas, and reallocation as verification reveals where marginal effort buys the most hidden-suite coverage.
